title: My Codex-assisted strategy game now has a Steam demo. Packaging needed its own checks.
author: va2k0r
selftext:
I posted about DeltaV here last week. Today I released its free demo on Steam for Windows and macOS. The video above shows the game.



I'm making it with TypeScript, Three.js and help from Codex. The Steam version uses Electron. The part I'd add to my previous post is that a working browser build and a working desktop package are separate things to verify.



The project has separate web and Steam builds, plus a tutorial-only demo. I keep the build mode and demo restrictions explicit so a change to the website doesn't quietly end up in the wrong distribution. The packaged app also needs its own startup and file-loading checks. A page opening in a browser doesn't prove the files inside the desktop app will load correctly.



That gave me a more useful way to work with the agent: ask for evidence from the actual package, alongside the code checks. The same goes for the tutorial. Correct rules aren't enough if a new player can't work out what to click.



DeltaV is a turn-based game where the whole fleet shares one fuel reserve. The demo is a guided tutorial:

[https://store.steampowered.com/app/5070120/](https://store.steampowered.com/app/5070120/)



For other people shipping games with coding agents, what did you add to your checks when you moved from a browser prototype to a downloadable build?

comments.author: _DDark_
comments.body: It looks cool, but would look cooler if I understood what the gameplay is. Nice vibes though! Wishlisted, will play the demo when I get time.

replies.author: va2k0r
replies.body:
Hello and thank you for reaching out!  
It's a turn based strategy game, celestial bodies either produce ships, fuel or nothing, the only weapon are missiles that takes days to reach the target so it's a dance between ships, missiles and planets.  
Try out the tutorial and see if you can complete it!
